citation_details.title: Transformer-Based Multimodal Time-Series Analysis for Stroke Rehabilitation: Bridging Behavioral Recovery and Neuroplasticity via Cross-Modal Self-Attention
citation_details.author: Yiyang Wen, Chongqing Shi
citation_details.venue: International Conference on Big Data and Intelligent Medicine (BDIMed)
citation_details.abstract: Post-stroke motor recovery is driven by neural plasticity. However, routine clinical practice records only intermittent behavioral outcomes and misses the underlying neurophysiological dynamics. This paper develops and optimizes a Transformer-based multimodal time-series framework that aims to close this gap. The framework jointly models kinematics, eye-tracking, and portable electroencephalography (EEG) acquired during standardized virtual-reality (VR) upper-limb tasks. Its computational core is a lightweight cross-modal Transformer encoder. The encoder uses learnable modality embeddings and a linear-attention (FAVOR+) approximation to fuse heterogeneous, asynchronously informative channels within a single 0.52-million-parameter model. It jointly predicts a continuous motor-function score (0–100, aligned with the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the Upper Extremity) and a three-state neuroplasticity-trend index. citation_details.title: Disentangling Confusable Actions in Multimodal HAR: A Stability-driven Feature Selection Framework for EEG and EMG-IMU
citation_details.author: Le Hoang Nhat Do, Ngoc Tuong Vy Le, Quoc Thai Le, Quoc Bao Trinh, Phi Hoai Nguyen, Nhat Ngoc Nguyen, Nhat Tan Le
citation_details.venue: International Conference on Activity and Behavior Computing (ABC)
citation_details.abstract: Upper-limb movement intention recognition from multimodal biological signals is a key enabling technology for motor-assistive systems and human-computer interaction, yet remains challenged by action ambiguity and inter-subject variability. This study investigates movement intention recognition from two complementary modalities EMG–IMU and EEG, under both subject-aware and cross-subject evaluation settings, with emphasis on how feature representations and evaluation protocols affect generalization. For EMG-IMU, we propose a recognition framework based on time-synchronized signal processing and multi-domain feature extraction, combined with a confusion-driven feature optimization strategy. By explicitly analyzing interclass confusion patterns, two feature sets are constructed for subject-aware and cross-subject scenarios. citation_details.title: Robust Cross-Session EEG Measurement via Trial-Conditioned Log-Euclidean Reference Synthesis
citation_details.author: Jinguo Huang, Xiong Xiong, Yunfei Xu, 翁心华, Li Su
citation_details.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
citation_details.abstract: Reliable longitudinal EEG systems require inference methods that remain stable when repeated EEG measurements are affected by cross-session nonstationarity. In practice, variations in electrode impedance, cap placement, and user state introduce substantial distribution shifts across days, while many existing decoding methods depend on daily recalibration or target-session statistics, increasing measurement burden and limiting routine use. We propose log-Euclidean anchor-prompt network (LEAPNet), a geometry-aware signal conditioning and representation framework for robust zero-shot cross-session EEG decoding. Its core is a trial-conditioned log-Euclidean (LE) reference synthesis mechanism, supported by learnable sinc bandpass filtering and analytically regularized Ledoit–Wolf covariance estimation for stable covariance representation under session drift. citation_details.title: Bayesian Complete-Pooling in Cross-Subject Classification for Motor Imagery Electroencephalogram
citation_details.author: Ethan Davis
citation_details.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have long sought calibration-free operation, yet classifiers are typically benchmarked on discrimination alone. Discrimination is blind to calibration, a meaningful gap given that electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are nonstationary and point-estimate classifiers can become overconfident under distribution shift. We conducted a large-scale study contrasting Bayesian complete-pooling models against frequentist baselines for cross-subject, left-hand versus right-hand motor imagery EEG classification across 20 datasets. Each of six frequentist pipelines was paired with an analogous Bayesian pipeline sharing identical feature engineering, fit via Markov chain Monte Carlo posterior sampling. Our primary metric was the Brier score, decomposed into reliability and resolution, alongside the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for discrimination and Shannon entropy for sharpness.
